newsitem.title: POLAND: E.Europe ripe for big portfolio inflows - analyst.
newsitem.headline: E.Europe ripe for big portfolio inflows - analyst.

text.p: Expanding Eastern and Central European equity markets and growing stability in the region are likely to spur portfolio investment by major Western funds, an independent Polish think-tank said on Thursday.

Janusz Dabrowski, deputy head of Instytut Badan nad Gospodarka Rynkowa, told a news conference foreign investment funds have been showing increased interest in the region's markets and expected competition for fresh funds to heat up.

"Until recently Eastern and Central European markets have been considered too shallow for large portfolio investments, but now they are considered broader, more stable and the countries' economies are strengthening," he said.
He added that the Polish market was especially highly valued by prospective investors as the one with the biggest potential in the region and operating in the stable economy.
Dabrowski said the market development so far made Warsaw well positioned to assume a role of a regional financial centre.
"The Polish market is well perceived, big funds are mulling entry...Warsaw will likely have to become the financial and capital centre of the region," he said.
